sections.label: Amending Registration of Criminals Act
sections.summary: MHA proposes amending the RCA to let a Singapore-designated authority share information with foreign law enforcement agencies on a reciprocal basis, with safeguards, to implement a US agreement and keep the US Visa-Waiver Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), therefore, proposes to amend the Registration of Criminals Act (RCA) to expressly allow a Singapore-designated authority to share such information with foreign law enforcement agencies, on a reciprocal basis, that is, the foreign agencies must be prepared to share similar information with our agencies on the same terms.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The transmission of information will be subject to stringent safeguards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This will also enable us to implement the Preventing and Combating Serious Crime Agreement with the United States of America (US) by allowing information-sharing between both governments for the prevention and combating of serious crimes, such as transnational organised crime and terrorism.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The implementation of this agreement enables us to continue to participate in the US Visa-Waiver Programme, which allows Singaporeans to travel to the US for tourism or business without the need for a visa.

sections.label: Grounds to refuse sharing information
sections.summary: Information requested will not be shared if it is contrary to Singapore's public interest, or may prejudice criminal investigation, criminal proceedings or any person's safety in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Third, we will not share the information requested, if it is contrary to Singapore's public interest, or may prejudice any criminal investigation or criminal proceedings in a Singapore Court Page: 77 or the safety of any person in Singapore.

sections.label: Taking particulars after bail release
sections.summary: The Bill amends sections 8 and 13B(1) to let law enforcement agencies take registrable particulars and body samples after a person is released on bail or personal bond.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The Bill amends sections 8 and 13B(1) to allow our law enforcement agencies to take the person's registrable particulars and body samples after the person has been released on bail or personal bond, whether by a Court or otherwise.

sections.label: Enhanced RCA and transnational crime cooperation
sections.summary: The enhanced RCA will allow the Police to better cooperate with the international community to prevent, detect and prosecute transnational crime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The enhanced RCA will allow the Police to better cooperate with the international community to prevent, detect and prosecute transnational crime.

sections.label: Verifying foreign agency conditions
sections.summary: The question asks to what extent due diligence will be exercised to verify whether a requesting foreign agency can fulfil the set conditions before information is furnished.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My question is: to what extent will we exercise due diligence to verify whether the foreign agency requesting the information is able to fulfil the conditions we have set, before we furnish the information requested?

sections.label: Ascertaining requesting country obligations
sections.summary: The question asks how the Government will ascertain whether a requesting country can fulfil the obligations expected of it under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How will the Government go about ascertaining whether a requesting country can fulfil the obligations we expect of them under the Bill?

sections.label: ASEAN crime information sharing safeguards
sections.summary: Asks what is being done to ensure ASEAN countries can share crime information while safeguarding it from abuse.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Given the different stages of development among ASEAN countries and each country's institutions, what has been done or is being done to ensure that ASEAN countries can, indeed, share crime information with one another, with the confidence that the information will be safeguarded and not abused?

sections.label: Sharing Register of Criminals data
sections.summary: Proposed amendments would let Register of Criminals information be shared with foreign law enforcement for crime prevention, investigation and prosecution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Through the proposed amendments in the Registration of Criminal (Amendment) Bill, information that is recorded in the Register of Criminals, such as fingerprints or photographs, can be shared with foreign law enforcement agencies for the prevention, investigation and prosecution of crimes regionally or, possibly, globally.

sections.label: CRO limits on registrable particulars
sections.summary: CRO currently lets authorised officers take registrable particulars only from arrested accused persons, not those on bail or bond under investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: At present, the CRO only allows authorised officers to take finger impressions, photographs and body samples of persons who are arrested and are accused of a crime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, authorised officers are not able to obtain these "registrable particulars" or body samples from individuals who have been released on bail or a personal bond but are still under investigation.

sections.label: Informing Registrar of acquittal
sections.summary: RCA requires the authorised officer to inform the Registrar immediately if a person whose particulars were taken is acquitted or discharged without conviction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For instance, RCA already provides that in the event that finger impressions, photographs, registrable particulars and body samples are taken from a person during an investigation, but the person is acquitted or discharged without a conviction being recorded against him, the authorised officer in-charge of the case shall immediately inform the Registrar of the acquittal or discharge.

sections.label: Arrest of 27 Bangladeshi nationals
sections.summary: Singapore's Internal Security Department arrested 27 male Bangladeshi nationals planning extremist activities in other countries, including Bangladesh.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the Internal Security Department recently arrested 27 male Bangladeshi nationals working in Singapore who were planning to take part in extremist activities in other countries, including Bangladesh, their home country.

sections.label: ECRIS and Malaysia-US database
sections.summary: ECRIS sees 288,000 requests yearly in the EU, and Malaysia and the US signed an agreement to share biometric records of about 1.2 million terrorism suspects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Since the introduction of ECRIS, 288,000 such requests are made every year across the EU.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Closer to home, also in response to the Paris terror attacks, Malaysia and the US governments signed an agreement in November 2015 to share a database containing the biometric records of about 1.2 million people suspected of terrorism and other serious crimes.

sections.label: Foreign agencies and criminal records
sections.summary: Asks how foreign law enforcement will protect confidentiality, prevent misuse of shared information, and whether Singaporeans abroad face unfair treatment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: How will foreign law enforcement agencies undertake to protect the confidentiality of information?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: How do we ensure that the information shared will not be abused for other purposes?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Will Singaporeans be unfairly treated when they work and live in other countries that have access to our criminal records?

sections.label: Register information sharing purposes
sections.summary: The Bill clarifies that register information can be shared only for specified purposes, enabling quicker and more effective action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Bill clarifies that register information can be shared for specified purposes only and this will enable us to act more quickly and effectively.

sections.label: Definition of foreign offence
sections.summary: A foreign offence is conduct against a foreign country's law that would be a Singapore offence punishable with over 12 months' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: A foreign offence is defined to mean an offence against the law of the foreign country, which if the conduct constituting the foreign offence had occurred in Singapore, would amount to an offence against the law of Singapore punishable with imprisonment for a term exceeding 12 months.

sections.label: Privacy concerns and confidentiality breaches
sections.summary: The Bill will reduce potential misuse of information, and Singapore will not take any breach of confidentiality lightly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Page: 84 We understand the privacy concerns associated with the sharing of information or data with foreign jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We would like to assure Members of the House that the Bill will reduce the potential for misuse of information, and Singapore will not take any breach of confidentiality lightly.

sections.label: No unrelated information disclosure
sections.summary: Singapore will not accede to requests for information for purposes unrelated to preventing and combating crime and terrorism, such as employment screening.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To be clear, we will not accede to any request for information to be disclosed for any purpose that is unrelated to the prevention and combating of crime and terrorism, such as for employment screening purposes.

sections.label: Criminal record and checkpoint checks
sections.summary: A criminal record does not automatically result in enhanced checks at checkpoints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: A criminal record does not automatically result in enhanced checks at checkpoints.

sections.label: Deletion of record after acquittal
sections.summary: The record will be deleted if there is a subsequent acquittal or if the conviction is rendered spent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: If there is a subsequent acquittal, or if the conviction is rendered spent, the record will be deleted.

sections.label: Bill improves international cooperation safeguards
sections.summary: The Bill will improve Singapore's ability to cooperate with international partners while ensuring appropriate safeguards are in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This Bill will improve Singapore's ability to cooperate with our international partners while ensuring appropriate safeguards are in place.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: I just have one clarification for the Senior Minister of State who mentioned in his round-up speech that each request will be assessed carefully and we may need to work with the foreign agency over a period of time to gain confidence in their capacity to fulfil the obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Our law enforcement agencies are frequently in touch with and cooperate with our ASEAN law enforcement partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In every jurisdiction, there are a range of enforcement agencies, and this is an ongoing process.
